questions.text: Which physical quantity is the measure of the inertia of a body?
questions.explanation: Mass is the measure of the inertia of a body.

questions.text: The SI unit of force is the ___.
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.text: Newton's second law of motion is expressed mathematically as ___.
questions.explanation: The second law gives F = ma.

questions.text: One newton is the force that gives a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of ___.
questions.explanation: F = ma = 1 kg × 1 m/s² = 1 N.

questions.text: Newton's first law of motion is also called the law of ___.
questions.explanation: The first law is known as the law of inertia.

questions.text: A book on a table stays there until it is pushed or pulled. This illustrates Newton's ___.
questions.explanation: The first law says a body at rest stays at rest unless a force acts on it.

questions.text: Newton's third law states that for every action there is ___.
questions.explanation: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

questions.text: Which of the following is an application of Newton's third law?
questions.explanation: The recoil of a gun is a classic example of action and reaction.

questions.text: Linear momentum is the product of ___.
questions.explanation: Momentum p = mv.

questions.text: The SI unit of linear momentum is ___.
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity, so its unit is kg m s⁻¹.

questions.text: Impulse is the product of ___.
questions.explanation: Impulse = force × time.

questions.text: The impulse of a force is numerically equal to the ___.
questions.explanation: Ft = mv − mu, the change in momentum.

questions.text: The SI unit of impulse is the ___.
questions.explanation: Impulse = force × time, hence N s.

questions.text: Linear momentum is conserved in a collision provided ___.
options: no external force acts on the system
the colliding bodies have equal masses
questions.explanation: Conservation of momentum holds when no external force acts on the system.

questions.text: In an elastic collision, besides momentum, which quantity is conserved?
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision both kinetic energy and momentum are conserved.

questions.text: When two bodies collide and stick together, the collision is said to be ___.
questions.explanation: Sticking together means a perfectly inelastic collision.

questions.text: The coefficient of restitution of a perfectly elastic collision is ___.
questions.explanation: e = 1 for a perfectly elastic collision.

questions.text: The coefficient of restitution of a perfectly inelastic collision is ___.
questions.explanation: e = 0 for a perfectly inelastic collision.

questions.text: Speed is the rate of change of ___ with time.
questions.explanation: Speed = distance travelled ÷ time taken.

questions.text: The unit of speed is ___.
questions.explanation: Speed is distance over time, measured in m s⁻¹.

questions.text: Velocity is the rate of change of ___ with time.
questions.explanation: Velocity = displacement ÷ time.

questions.text: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction.

questions.text: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed is described by magnitude only.

questions.text: Acceleration is the rate of change of ___ with time.
questions.explanation: Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time.

questions.text: The unit of acceleration is ___.
questions.explanation: Acceleration is velocity per unit time, giving m s⁻².

questions.text: A negative acceleration is called ___.
questions.explanation: Negative acceleration is retardation or deceleration.

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is about ___.
For a body thrown vertically upward, the acceleration due to gravity is taken to be ___.
questions.explanation: For upward motion g is negative.

questions.text: At its maximum height, the velocity of a body thrown vertically upward is ___.
questions.explanation: At maximum height the body is momentarily at rest, v = 0.

questions.text: The first equation of motion under constant acceleration is ___.
questions.explanation: v = u + at is the first equation of motion.

questions.text: The second equation of motion is ___.
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² is the second equation of motion.

questions.text: The third equation of motion is ___.
questions.explanation: v² = u² + 2as is the third equation of motion.

questions.text: A body that covers equal displacements in equal intervals of time moves with ___.
questions.explanation: Equal displacements in equal times mean uniform velocity.

questions.text: If v = u + at with u = 0, a = 2 m/s² and t = 3 s, the value of v is ___.
Using s = ut + ½at² with u = 0, a = 4 m/s² and t = 2 s gives s = ___.
A speed of 50 km/h is approximately equal to ___.
A car moves at 60 m/s and a motorbike ahead of it moves at 95 m/s in the same direction. The velocity of the bike relative to the car is ___.
questions.explanation: V_relative = 95 − 60 = 35 m/s.

questions.text: Work done = force × ___ measured in the direction of the force.
questions.explanation: Work = force × displacement in the direction of the force.

questions.text: The SI unit of work is the ___.
questions.explanation: Work is measured in joules (J).

questions.text: When the displacement is perpendicular to the applied force (θ = 90°), the work done is ___.
questions.explanation: W = Fs cos 90° = 0.

questions.text: The kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with velocity v is ___.
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv².

questions.text: The gravitational potential energy of a mass m at a height h is ___.
questions.explanation: PE = mgh.

questions.text: The elastic potential energy stored in a stretched spring of force constant k and extension x is ___.
questions.explanation: Elastic PE = ½kx².

questions.text: Energy is the ___ of a body.
questions.explanation: Energy is the ability to do work.

questions.text: The work-energy theorem states that the net work done on a body equals its change in ___.
questions.explanation: W_net = ΔKE.

questions.text: Power is the ___.
questions.explanation: Power = work done per unit time.

questions.text: The SI unit of power is the ___.
questions.explanation: Power is measured in watts (W).

questions.text: One horse power (hp) is equal to ___.
questions.explanation: 1 hp = 746 watts.

questions.text: The instantaneous power delivered by a force F to a body moving with velocity v is ___.
questions.explanation: P = dW/dt = Fv.

questions.text: When only conservative forces act on a system, the total mechanical energy ___.
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy is conserved when only conservative forces act.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental (base) quantity?
questions.explanation: Velocity is a derived quantity.

questions.text: The SI unit of length is the ___.
questions.explanation: Length is measured in metres (m).

questions.text: The SI unit of mass is the ___.
questions.explanation: Mass is measured in kilograms (kg).

questions.text: The SI unit of time is the ___.
questions.explanation: Time is measured in seconds (s).

questions.text: The SI unit of temperature is the ___.
questions.explanation: Kelvin (K) is the SI unit of temperature.

questions.text: How many fundamental (base) quantities are there in the SI system?
questions.explanation: There are seven fundamental quantities.

questions.text: The dimension of length is written as ___.
questions.explanation: Length has dimension [L].

questions.text: The dimension of mass is written as ___.
questions.explanation: Mass has dimension [M].

questions.text: The dimension of time is written as ___.
questions.explanation: Time has dimension [T].

questions.text: The dimension of force is ___.
questions.explanation: Force = mass × acceleration, giving [MLT⁻²].

questions.text: The dimension of velocity is ___.
questions.explanation: Velocity = length/time, giving [LT⁻¹].

questions.text: The dimension of acceleration is ___.
questions.explanation: Acceleration is velocity per unit time, giving [LT⁻²].

questions.text: The dimension of density is ___.
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume, giving [ML⁻³].

questions.text: The dimension of pressure (stress) is ___.
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area, giving [ML⁻¹T⁻²].

questions.text: Which of the following quantities is dimensionless?
questions.explanation: Angles and trigonometric functions have no dimension.

questions.text: The magnitude of a unit vector is ___.
questions.explanation: A unit vector has magnitude 1.

questions.text: By definition, one metre is the distance travelled by light in a vacuum in ___.
questions.explanation: The metre is defined using the distance light travels in 1/299 792 458 s.

questions.text: A vector quantity is fully described by ___.
questions.explanation: Vectors have both magnitude and direction.

questions.text: The dimension of area is ___.
questions.explanation: Area = length × breadth, giving [L²].

questions.text: The dimension of volume is ___.
questions.explanation: Volume = length cubed, giving [L³].

questions.text: Density is defined as the ___.
questions.explanation: Density = mass ÷ volume.

questions.text: The SI unit of density is ___.
questions.explanation: Density is measured in kg/m³.

questions.text: The density of water is ___.
questions.explanation: Water has a density of 1000 kg/m³.

questions.text: The square metre (m²) is the SI unit of ___.
questions.explanation: Area is measured in square metres.

questions.text: A physical quantity is expressed as its magnitude multiplied by its ___.
questions.explanation: Measurement = magnitude × unit.

questions.text: The horizontal component of a vector A making an angle θ with the x-axis is ___.
questions.explanation: Ax = A cos θ.

questions.text: The vertical component of a vector A is ___.
questions.explanation: Ay = A sin θ.

questions.text: The magnitude of a vector with components Ax and Ay is ___.
questions.explanation: |A| = √(Ax² + Ay²) by Pythagoras' theorem.

questions.text: 2π radians is equal to ___.
questions.explanation: 2π rad = 360° = 1 revolution.

questions.text: The sum of the squares of the direction cosines of a vector equals ___.
questions.explanation: cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ = 1.

questions.text: The SI unit of angular displacement is the ___.
questions.explanation: Angular displacement is measured in radians.

questions.text: Angular velocity is the rate of change of ___ with time.
questions.explanation: Angular velocity = angular displacement ÷ time.

questions.text: The unit of angular velocity is ___.
questions.explanation: Angular velocity is measured in rad/s.

questions.text: The relationship between linear velocity v and angular velocity ω is ___.
questions.explanation: v = ωr.

questions.text: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of ___ with time.
questions.explanation: Angular acceleration = change in angular velocity ÷ time.

questions.text: The unit of angular acceleration is ___.
questions.explanation: Angular acceleration is measured in rad/s².

questions.text: The circular-motion analogue of the equation v = u + at is ___.
questions.explanation: ω = ω₀ + αt is the analogue of v = u + at.

questions.text: Centripetal acceleration is given by ___.
questions.explanation: ac = v²/r.

questions.text: Centripetal acceleration can also be expressed as ___.
questions.explanation: ac = rω² since v = ωr.

questions.text: The centripetal force acting on a mass m moving with speed v in a circle of radius r is ___.
questions.explanation: Fc = mv²/r.

questions.text: Centripetal force on a body in circular motion always acts ___.
options: towards the centre of the circle
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is directed towards the centre.

questions.text: The force that appears to act on a body in circular motion away from the centre is the ___.
questions.explanation: Centrifugal force acts away from the centre of rotation.

questions.text: One complete revolution of a body in a circular path equals ___.
questions.explanation: A full circle is 2π radians.

questions.text: For a body making one revolution in time T, its angular velocity ω is ___.
questions.explanation: ω = 2π/T.

questions.text: The frequency f of an oscillation is related to its period T by ___.
questions.explanation: Frequency is the reciprocal of the period.

questions.text: The relationship between angular velocity and frequency is ___.
questions.explanation: ω = 2πf.

questions.text: If the speed of a body moving in a circle of fixed radius is doubled, the centripetal force becomes ___.
questions.explanation: F ∝ v², so doubling v makes the force 4 times as large.

questions.text: The work done by the centripetal force on a body moving round a circle is ___.
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is perpendicular to the displacement, so it does no work.

questions.text: A car rounding a circular race track is kept on the track by the ___.
questions.explanation: The centripetal force pulls the car towards the centre of the track.

questions.text: The device used in industry and hospitals to separate heavier liquids from lighter ones by spinning is the ___.
questions.explanation: A centrifuge uses centrifugal force to separate liquids of different densities.

questions.text: In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration of the body is proportional to ___.
questions.explanation: a = −ω²x, so acceleration is proportional to displacement.

questions.text: The maximum displacement of an oscillating body from its equilibrium position is its ___.
questions.explanation: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from equilibrium.

questions.text: The time taken for one complete vibration of an oscillating body is its ___.
questions.explanation: Period is the time for one complete vibration.

questions.text: The number of complete oscillations made per unit time is the ___.
questions.explanation: Frequency is the number of vibrations per unit time.

questions.text: The period of a simple pendulum of length l is ___.
The period of a mass m oscillating on a spring of force constant k is ___.
The maximum velocity of a body performing SHM with amplitude A and angular velocity ω is ___.
questions.explanation: v_max = ωA.

questions.text: The total energy of a body performing SHM is proportional to ___.
questions.explanation: E = ½mω²A², so E ∝ A².

questions.text: At the equilibrium position of a body performing SHM, its acceleration is ___.
questions.explanation: a = −ω²x and x = 0 at equilibrium, so a = 0.

questions.text: A body moves in a circle of radius 3 m with angular velocity 2 rad/s. Its linear speed is ___.
Newton's law of universal gravitation states that the force between two masses is ___.
options: proportional to the sum of the masses
proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them
inversely proportional to the product of the masses
independent of the distance between them
questions.explanation: F = GMm/r².

questions.text: In the equation F = GMm/r², the symbol G stands for the ___.
questions.explanation: G is the universal gravitational constant.

questions.text: The value of the universal gravitational constant G is about ___.
questions.explanation: G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg².

questions.text: The gravitational force between any two masses is always ___.
questions.explanation: Gravitation is always an attractive force.

questions.text: The equation g = GM/r² gives the ___.
options: acceleration due to gravity at the earth's surface
questions.explanation: g = GM/r² is the gravitational field strength on the surface.

questions.text: The weight w of a body of mass m is given by ___.
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × acceleration due to gravity.

questions.text: The gravitational potential at a point a distance r from the centre of mass M is ___.
questions.explanation: V = −GM/r, taking the potential at infinity as zero.

questions.text: The escape velocity from the earth's surface is given by ___.
The escape velocity from the surface of the earth is approximately ___.
questions.explanation: With g = 9.8 m/s² and r = 6.4 × 10⁶ m, v_e ≈ 11 km/s.

questions.text: Gravitational field strength is defined as the ___.
options: force per unit mass at a point in the field
questions.explanation: Field strength = force per unit mass.

questions.text: Kepler's first law states that planets move in ___ orbits with the Sun at one focus.
questions.explanation: Planetary orbits are ellipses.

questions.text: Kepler's second law states that a line from the Sun to a planet ___.
options: sweeps equal angles in equal times
sweeps out equal areas in equal times
covers equal distances in equal times
questions.explanation: Equal areas are swept out in equal times.

questions.text: Kepler's third law states that the square of the period of a planet is proportional to ___.
options: the cube of its mean distance from the Sun
its mean distance from the Sun
the square of its mean distance
questions.explanation: T² ∝ r³.

questions.text: The gravitational force between two bodies separated by a distance r is 100 N. If the separation is doubled, the force becomes ___.
If one of two attracting masses is halved while the distance stays constant, the gravitational force becomes ___.
questions.explanation: F ∝ m, so halving one mass halves the force.

questions.text: Which planet in the solar system has the most eccentric orbit?
questions.explanation: Mercury has the most eccentric orbit.

questions.text: The weight of a body of mass 1 kg on the earth's surface is about ___.
The gravitational constant G was first measured in the laboratory by ___.
questions.explanation: Cavendish measured G in 1798.

questions.text: A satellite moving in a circular orbit of radius r around the earth has orbital speed ___.
questions.explanation: v_s = √(gr).

questions.text: A body weighing 560 N on the earth's surface is moved to a distance from the earth's centre equal to twice the earth's radius. Its weight there is ___.
questions.explanation: g falls by a factor of 4, so 560/4 = 140 N.

questions.text: Elasticity is the property of a material to ___.
options: return to its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed
flow freely when a force is applied
questions.explanation: An elastic material regains its original shape when the load is removed.

questions.text: Hooke's law states that, within the elastic limit, the applied force F is proportional to the ___.
questions.explanation: F ∝ e, so F = ke.

questions.text: In Hooke's law F = kx, the constant k is called the ___.
questions.explanation: k is the force (stiffness) constant of the spring.

questions.text: Stress is defined as the ___.
options: force per unit area (restoring force per unit area)
questions.explanation: Stress = force per unit area.

questions.text: Strain is defined as the ___.
questions.explanation: Strain = extension ÷ original length.

questions.text: Strain is a quantity that is ___.
questions.explanation: Strain is a ratio of lengths, so it has no unit.

questions.text: Young's modulus is the ratio of ___.
questions.explanation: Young's modulus = tensile stress ÷ tensile strain.

questions.text: The strain energy stored in a stretched wire is given by ___.
questions.explanation: Strain energy = ½Fe = ½ke².

questions.text: Strain energy per unit volume of a stretched material equals ___.
questions.explanation: E_v = ½ × stress × strain.

questions.text: The three elastic moduli are Young's modulus, bulk modulus and ___.
questions.explanation: The three moduli are Young's, bulk and shear moduli.

questions.text: Tensile (normal) stress acts ___ to the plane of the surface.
questions.explanation: Normal (tensile) stress acts perpendicular to the surface.

questions.text: Shear stress acts ___ to the plane of the surface.
questions.explanation: Shear stress acts parallel (tangentially) to the surface.

questions.text: Pressure is defined as the ___.
options: force acting perpendicularly per unit area
questions.explanation: Pressure = perpendicular force per unit area.

questions.text: The SI unit of pressure is the ___.
questions.explanation: Pa = N/m² (one newton per square metre).

questions.text: The hydrostatic pressure at a depth h in a liquid of density ρ is given by ___.
questions.explanation: P = ρgh.

questions.text: In a liquid at rest, the pressure ___ with depth.
questions.explanation: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth.

questions.text: The relative density of a substance is the ratio of its density to the density of ___.
questions.explanation: Relative density is measured against the density of water.

questions.text: Archimedes' principle states that the upthrust on a body immersed in a fluid is equal to ___.
options: the weight of the fluid displaced by the body
questions.explanation: Upthrust equals the weight of the fluid displaced.

questions.text: A body floats in a liquid when the buoyant force is ___.
options: greater than or equal to its weight
questions.explanation: The body floats when buoyancy is at least as large as its weight.

questions.text: A body sinks in a liquid when its ___.
options: weight is greater than the buoyant force
weight is less than the buoyant force
questions.explanation: The body sinks when mg > buoyant force.

questions.text: In laminar (streamline) flow, the fluid moves ___.
options: smoothly in parallel layers without intermixing
questions.explanation: Laminar flow is smooth parallel-layer flow below the critical velocity.

questions.text: Turbulent flow occurs when the velocity of a fluid ___.
questions.explanation: Above the critical velocity the flow becomes turbulent.

questions.text: For a Reynolds number Re less than 2000, the flow is ___.
questions.explanation: Re < 2000 gives laminar flow.

questions.text: For a Reynolds number Re greater than 4000, the flow is ___.
questions.explanation: Re > 4000 gives turbulent flow.

questions.text: Viscosity is a measure of a fluid's ___.
questions.explanation: Viscosity measures the fluid's resistance to flow.

questions.text: When the temperature of a liquid increases, its viscosity ___.
questions.explanation: Viscosity decreases as temperature increases.

questions.text: Stokes' law gives the viscous drag on a sphere of radius r moving with velocity v in a fluid of viscosity η as ___.
questions.explanation: F = 6πηrv.

questions.text: At terminal velocity, the acceleration of a falling sphere through a viscous liquid is ___.
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity the net force is zero, so a = 0.

questions.text: Terminal velocity is reached when the viscous drag on the falling body just balances the ___.
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, viscous drag balances weight and upthrust.

questions.text: Surface tension is the force acting ___ per unit length of an imaginary line drawn on the liquid surface.
questions.explanation: Surface tension acts tangentially to the liquid surface.

questions.text: The SI unit of surface tension is ___.
questions.explanation: Surface tension = force per unit length, measured in N/m.

questions.text: The surface of a liquid behaves like ___.
questions.explanation: Surface tension makes the liquid surface act like a stretched elastic skin.

questions.text: Surface tension of a liquid ___ when its temperature increases.
questions.explanation: Heating weakens the intermolecular forces, lowering surface tension.

questions.text: Adding soap or detergent to water ___ its surface tension.
questions.explanation: Soap (an impurity) lowers the surface tension of water.

questions.text: The excess pressure inside a liquid drop of surface tension γ and radius r is ___.
questions.explanation: A liquid drop has one surface, so excess pressure = 2γ/r.

questions.text: Because a soap bubble has two liquid surfaces, its excess pressure is ___.
questions.explanation: A soap bubble has two surfaces, giving excess pressure = 4γ/r.

questions.text: Adhesion is the force of attraction between molecules of ___.
questions.explanation: Adhesion acts between unlike substances, e.g. water and glass.

questions.text: Cohesion is the force of attraction between molecules of ___.
questions.explanation: Cohesion acts between identical molecules.

questions.text: Water rises in a narrow glass capillary tube mainly because of the ___.
options: adhesive force between water and glass
questions.explanation: Capillary rise is due to adhesion between water and glass.

questions.text: Water rises 2 cm in a capillary tube of radius r. In a tube of radius r/3, the same water will rise to ___.
questions.explanation: hr is constant, so h₂ = 3 × 2 = 6 cm.

questions.text: Most solids and liquids ___ when their temperature is increased.
questions.explanation: Heating increases molecular vibration, so solids and liquids expand.

questions.text: The increase in length of a solid rod on heating is given by ___.
questions.explanation: ΔL = αLiΔT.

questions.text: The coefficient of linear expansion α is measured in ___.
questions.explanation: The unit of α is 1/°C.

questions.text: The coefficient of area (superficial) expansion of a solid is related to its linear expansivity α by ___.
questions.explanation: Area expansivity = 2α.

questions.text: The coefficient of volume (cubic) expansion of a solid is related to its linear expansivity α by ___.
questions.explanation: Cubic expansivity = 3α.

questions.text: The increase in volume of a liquid on heating is given by ___.
questions.explanation: ΔV = βViΔT.

questions.text: A brass rod 3 cm long at 0°C (α = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵/°C) is heated to 100°C. Its increase in length is ___.
10 litres of mercury (β = 1.8 × 10⁻⁴/°C) is heated through 30°C. Its increase in volume is ___.
A bimetallic strip is commonly used in a ___.
questions.explanation: Bimetallic strips are used in thermostats.

questions.text: Gaps are left between railway rails mainly to ___.
options: allow for the contraction of trains
allow for the expansion of the rails when heated
questions.explanation: The gaps accommodate thermal expansion of the rails.

questions.text: Heat is best described as ___.
options: thermal energy in transit from a hotter body to a colder body
the total kinetic energy of a body
the internal energy stored in a body
questions.explanation: Heat is thermal energy in transit due to a temperature difference.

questions.text: Heat always flows from the body at ___.
options: lower temperature to the body at higher temperature
the same temperature to a colder one
higher temperature to the body at lower temperature
questions.explanation: Heat flows from hot to cold.

questions.text: The SI unit of heat is the ___.
questions.explanation: Heat is measured in joules (J).

questions.text: 1 calorie is approximately equal to ___.
Temperature is a measure of the ___ of a body.
questions.explanation: Temperature measures hotness or coldness.

questions.text: The zeroth law of thermodynamics states that if A and B are each in thermal equilibrium with C, then ___.
options: A and B cannot be in equilibrium
A and B are in thermal equilibrium with each other
heat flows from A to B
questions.explanation: Thermal equilibrium is transitive by the zeroth law.

questions.text: On the Celsius scale, the lower fixed point is ___.
questions.explanation: The ice point is 0°C.

questions.text: On the Fahrenheit scale, the upper fixed point is ___.
questions.explanation: The steam point is 212°F.

questions.text: The fundamental interval on the Fahrenheit scale is ___.
The SI unit of thermodynamic temperature is the ___.
questions.explanation: Kelvin (K) is the SI unit of temperature.

questions.text: A temperature of 20°C is equal to about ___.
A temperature of 50°C is equal to ___ on the Fahrenheit scale.
Absolute zero (0 K) is equal to about ___.
The triple point of water is defined as ___.
questions.explanation: The triple point of water is 273.16 K.

questions.text: Latent heat of fusion is the heat required to change ___ at constant temperature.
questions.explanation: Fusion is the solid-to-liquid change.

questions.text: Latent heat of vaporization is the heat required to change ___ at constant temperature.
questions.explanation: Vaporization is the liquid-to-vapour change.

questions.text: During melting or boiling of a pure substance, its temperature ___.
questions.explanation: Temperature stays constant during a change of state.

questions.text: The main mode of heat transfer in solids is ___.
questions.explanation: Conduction is the main mode of heat transfer in solids.

questions.text: The main mode of heat transfer in fluids (liquids and gases) is ___.
questions.explanation: Convection by moving fluid particles dominates in fluids.

questions.text: Heat from the sun reaches the earth by ___.
questions.explanation: Radiant heat travels through space at the speed of light.
